ratings_why.fun: Old Will, Black-Water Reflection and Follette make their carry kill their carry, and Hoard Mere hands you half of it; the Lost economy cards (Mapseller, Spunkie, Steward) are one-job filler around that chain.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because the tribe's damage is the enemy's own: every hit goes back onto their side, so it scales with the lobby's biggest boards, which no current tribe or generic auto-battler tribe does.

verdict_why: The v2 rules for Lost, self-hits and the Reflection now read cleanly; further passes would mostly reshuffle the Lost cards, not improve the chains.

points.text: Gaffer Turncoat's swap on a 3/20 triple-Lantern carrier is the best off-label trick here; letting the swap also target a Turnip-holding unit from another tribe would push the splash further.
Captain Spunkie is a 1/9 that Turncoat turns into a 9/1 that never attacks; a line where swapped Spunkie may attack would turn a dead pairing into a joke combo.
Sunken Causeway Lights makes leaving gaps a real choice, against fewer units deciding who attacks first; that tension is good and worth keeping visible when the Stones' timing is settled.
Three Start of Turn cards read Lost the same way; one of them reading drowns instead of Lost would add another axis without new keywords.
Ignis Fatuus has no cap while Stones, Follette, Tiddy Mun and the Barn Owl all add misleads; that is the hot payoff, so leave it and let the owner tune it.

standouts.why: Old Will turns every misled attack onto their biggest unit, which links Reflection, Follette and Hoard Mere into one drowning chain.
Black-Water Reflection doubles both sides of a hit that is all enemy damage; with enemy Cleave it is a board wipe.
Hoard Mere Light steals half of what their carry did to their other carry; drowning by return hits counts too.

weakest.why: Fresh-Ink Mapseller is plain gold from a count, with no interaction beyond more misleads.
Hobby Lantern is a vanilla carrier; fine as the base, but it does nothing else.
Brass-Badge Steward repeats Joan's job off the same Lost count.

flags.note: Ignis Fatuus gains per mislead with no cap; a Stones and Follette board could give 15+ misleads, about 90+ stats a turn.
Stingy Jack plus Joan and Steward toward a 12-Lantern front row could stall the enemy two cycles; the design names the brake.
Whether Stepping Stones count toward which side attacks first is not settled.
